docs.title: CLUTRO
docs.text:
Modern clustering toolkit for Go. Cluster sparse or dense rows with repeated bisection or spherical k-means, optimize a real criterion function, explain every cluster by its features, and get the same answer every time.

CLUTRO brings the ideas that made CLUTO the standard tool for document clustering — criterion-driven partitioning, repeated bisection, cluster interpretation — to a pure-Go library with no dependencies, context.Context cancellation, and a tested determinism contract.

Independent implementation

CLUTRO is inspired by CLUTO and implements the published algorithms from scratch. It is not affiliated with, derived from, or endorsed by the Karypis lab or the University of Minnesota.

docs.title: A first look
docs.text:
m, _ := matrix.NewCSRFromTriplets(nRows, nCols, triplets)
m.NormalizeRowsL2()

res, err := clutro.Fit(ctx, m,
    clutro.WithAlgorithm(clutro.RepeatedBisection),
    clutro.WithClusters(12),
    clutro.WithRefinement(true),  // CLUTO "rbr"
    clutro.WithSeed(42),
    clutro.WithColumnLabels(vocab),
)
for k := range res.K {
    fmt.Println(res.Sizes()[k], res.Describe(k, 5)) // top terms per cluster
}

clutro vcluster -clmethod=rbr -rowmodel=l2 docs.mat 50   # writes docs.mat.clustering.50
clutro evaluate docs.mat.clustering.50 docs.rclass        # ARI, NMI, purity, entropy

docs.title: Why CLUTRO
docs.text:
• Sparse-first. CSR matrices with float32 values; 100k-row TF-IDF corpora fit in memory and cluster in seconds.
  • The right objective. Spherical k-means and repeated bisection maximize I2 (Σ‖D_k‖), the criterion that works for cosine geometry, with refinement that moves single rows while it improves.
  • Explained clusters. Descriptive and discriminating features, representative rows, and internal/external similarity per cluster.
  • Deterministic. Same input, same seed, same version ⇒ same labels, whatever GOMAXPROCS is. Optimized paths are tested against slow reference implementations.
  • CLUTO-compatible where it matters. The same file formats, flag names and defaults, validated against CLUTO's own outputs on 103 real corpora.
  • Zero dependencies, library and CLI alike.

docs.title: Algorithms
docs.text:
All algorithms share partition.Options (exposed through clutro.With…): similarity, criterion, trials, max iterations, seed, workers, selection policy, refinement.

Algorithm clutro CLUTO What it does Repeated bisection RepeatedBisection rb Split one cluster at a time with a 2-way spherical k-means (several seeded trials), choosing the cluster by SelectBest (largest criterion gain) or SelectLargest, until k clusters exist. Returns a tree. Default. Repeated bisection + refinement RepeatedBisection + WithRefinement(true) rbr As above, then criterion-driven single-row moves over the k-way result. Typically 1–4% better criterion than rb. Direct Direct direct k-means++ seeding and Lloyd iterations for all k at once, then refinement. k-means KMeans — k-means++ and Lloyd only. Spherical k-means under cosine; classic under Euclidean.

docs.title: Seeding
docs.text: k-means and every bisection start from greedy k-means++: each new center is chosen among 2 + ln(k) candidates drawn by D² sampling, keeping the one that lowers the total potential most (as scikit-learn does). On text with cosine geometry, plain k-means++ has weak contrast (distances cluster around 0.7–0.95) and found the planted structure of a 6-cluster test corpus only 17% of the time per trial; greedy seeding raised that to 47%. With the default 10 trials the chance of missing it is below 0.2%.

docs.title: Trials
docs.text: Each k-means or bisection runs Trials times (default 10) from independent seeded streams and keeps the partition with the best criterion value. Trials are independent, so running them in parallel is a pure optimization; the result must not change.

docs.title: Lloyd iterations
docs.text: Rows are assigned to the composite they are most similar to; ties break to the lowest cluster index; rows are visited in index order; the assignment sweep is parallel but writes positionally. Empty clusters are reseeded with the row least similar to its own composite — deterministically.

docs.title: Choosing
docs.text:
• Text, TF-IDF, cosine: RepeatedBisection with refinement. Choose k ≈ rows/12 for "related items" boxes, or bisect further and CutMaxSize.
  • Dense embeddings: RepeatedBisection or KMeans under cosine after normalizing rows; Direct when k is small and you want the fastest k-way answer.
  • Euclidean data: KMeans or Direct with metric.Euclidean{}.
  • Unknown k: bisect to a generous k and cut the tree.

docs.title: Complexity
docs.text: Bisection is O(trials · iterations · n_cluster · nnz) per split; the whole tree is roughly O(k · trials · iterations · n · nnz / k) = O(trials · iterations · n · nnz) — linear in the data for a fixed k. Refinement is O(passes · n · k · nnz). On a laptop, 103 real corpora (up to 6,416 rows, 96k nonzeros, k = 535) cluster in 6 s with rb and 15 s with rbr.

docs.title: Agreement with CLUTO on 103 text corpora
docs.text:
A private set of 103 CLUTO runs (the doc2mat inputs and the .clustering.<k> files vcluster wrote, k = n/12 + 1, corpora from 4 to 6,416 rows and up to 96,630 nonzeros) was re-clustered with clutro golden:

Run Wall time, all 103 Mean ARI Mean NMI I2(CLUTRO)/I2(CLUTO) rb, -rowmodel l2 6.4 s 0.303 0.564 1.0007 rb, -rowmodel l2 -colmodel idf 6.2 s 0.351 0.591 0.959 rbr, -rowmodel l2 15.4 s 0.382 0.629 1.0333 CLUTRO rb seed 2 vs seed 1 — 0.484 0.684 0.9999
  • Under CLUTO's objective (colmodel none), CLUTRO matches (rb) or beats (rbr, +3.3%) the reference partitions.
  • Label agreement is partial by nature of the problem; CLUTRO disagrees with itself across seeds at a similar order (0.48).
  • The sub-1 ratio under idf shows the references were produced without column weighting — CLUTO's default.

docs.title: CLI Reference
docs.text:
go install github.com/grokify/clutro/cmd/clutro@latest

Flags are parsed with Go's standard library, so CLUTO-style -flag=value and -flag value work, as does --flag value.

docs.title: vcluster [flags] <matrix> <k>
docs.text:
Reads a CLUTO sparse or dense matrix file, clusters its rows into k clusters and writes <matrix>.clustering.<k> (one 0-based cluster id per row). Prints the shape, the criterion value and the cluster sizes.

Flag Default Values -clmethod rb rb, rbr, direct, kmeans -crfun i2 i2 -sim cos cos, euclid -cstype best best, largest — which cluster to bisect next -rowmodel none none, l2 — row scaling before clustering -colmodel none none, idf — column weighting (sparse only) -ntrials 10 seeded starts per k-means or bisection -niter 20 max k-means iterations and refinement passes -seed 0 seed for every random choice -parallel 0 worker count; 0 = all CPUs; results do not depend on it -clustfile <matrix>.clustering.<k> output path -json off print the result as JSON (shape, method, criterion, sizes, labels) instead of writing a file -showtree off print the bisection tree (rb/rbr)

docs.title: evaluate [flags] <clustering> <truth>
docs.text: Prints ARI, NMI, purity and entropy of a .clustering file against truth: another clustering file, or an .rclass file of one class name per line (-rclass, implied by the extension).

docs.title: golden [flags] <dir>
docs.text:
For every <name>.clustering.<k> in dir whose matrix <name> exists, re-clusters the matrix with repeated bisection into k clusters and prints a table of ARI, NMI and the I2 of the reference and CLUTRO partitions, with means. Corpora whose reference does not fit the matrix are skipped and listed on stderr.

Flag Default -seed 0 -ntrials 10 -parallel 0 -refine off -rowmodel l2 -colmodel none

docs.title: Exit codes
docs.text: 0 on success; 1 on bad arguments, unreadable or malformed files, or an error during clustering, with the reason on stderr.

docs.title: CLUTO Compatibility
docs.text: CLUTRO aims for algorithmic compatibility with CLUTO — the same objectives, the same algorithms, comparable results — and for file and command-line compatibility where that lets existing work carry over. It does not aim for bit-identical output: CLUTO's random number stream cannot be reproduced, and two correct implementations of a stochastic optimizer find different optima of equal quality.

docs.title: File formats (cluto package)
docs.text: File Format CLUTRO sparse matrix nrows ncols nnz, then col val pairs per row, 1-based columns, any order within a row, blank line = empty row cluto.ReadSparse, cluto.WriteSparse dense matrix nrows ncols, then one row of values per line cluto.ReadMatrix, cluto.WriteDense .clabel, .rlabel one column / row label per line cluto.ReadLabels, cluto.WriteLabels .rclass one class per row cluto.ReadLabels + cluto.ClassLabels .clustering.<k> one 0-based id per row, -1 unassigned cluto.ReadClustering, cluto.WriteClustering

docs.text: CLUTO CLUTRO Notes -clmethod=rb\|rbr\|direct same kmeans added -crfun=i2 same I1, E1, G1, G1′, H1, H2 are roadmap v0.2 -sim=cos same euclid added -cstype=best\|largest same feature-subspace selection not implemented -rowmodel=none same; l2 CLUTO normalizes rows internally for cosine; pass -rowmodel l2 on raw counts -colmodel=none\|idf same -ntrials=10, -niter=20 same defaults -seed same different stream -clustfile same -showfeatures, -showsummaries library (Describe, Summaries); CLI planned -fulltree, agglo roadmap v0.2 scluster (graph input) roadmap v0.3

docs.title: How close are the results?
docs.text:
On 103 real text corpora clustered by CLUTO with its defaults (rb, i2, cos, k = n/12 + 1), re-clustering with CLUTRO gives:

Mean ARI vs CLUTO I2(CLUTRO)/I2(CLUTO) rb 0.30 1.0007 rbr 0.38 1.033 CLUTRO rb seed 2 vs seed 1 0.48 0.9999

The partitions differ in detail — with k ≈ n/12 there are hundreds of small clusters and many optima of equal quality, which is why even two CLUTRO seeds agree only at ARI 0.48 — but under the objective CLUTO optimized, CLUTRO's partitions are as good or better. Eight of these corpora are published as numeric fixtures in testdata/cluto and the band is asserted by go test. See Benchmarks and Validation.

docs.title: Known differences
docs.text:
• Seeding. CLUTRO uses greedy k-means++; CLUTO samples initial centroids differently. Both run multiple trials and keep the best criterion.
  • Refinement scope. CLUTRO's rbr refines the final k-way partition; CLUTO also refines after each bisection. Per-level refinement is a v0.2 option.
  • Determinism. CLUTRO's results are independent of thread count by design; see Numerics and Determinism.
  • Not reimplemented: gCLUTO, scluster, the agglomerative methods, feature-subspace cluster selection. Density methods are out of scope; examples/hdbscan shows how to hand CLUTRO data to a density clusterer.

docs.title: Rows, not points
docs.text:
Every algorithm reads data through one small interface:

type Rows interface {
    NumRows() int
    NumCols() int
    Row(i int) SparseVec   // sorted column indices + float32 values
    RowNorm(i int) float32 // cached L2 norm
}

matrix.CSR is the sparse implementation (compressed sparse row, float32 values, uint32 columns); matrix.Dense is row-major dense storage whose rows are exposed as sparse views sharing one index slice. A caller with a memory-mapped or columnar store can implement Rows directly.

Values are stored as float32 and accumulated in float64. Cosine similarities on normalized rows stay accurate to well beyond single precision in practice; see Numerics.

docs.title: Similarity
docs.text: Algorithms are written against metric.Similarity. Cosine is the default and is a plain dot product on L2-normalized rows. Euclidean is exposed as a similarity 1/(1+d) so k-means can use it, with the true distance available too. Normalize rows (NormalizeRowsL2, or -rowmodel l2) before using cosine; CLUTO does this implicitly.

docs.title: Composite vectors
docs.text: A cluster's composite is the sum of its rows, kept dense in float64 with its norm maintained incrementally. Adding or removing a row costs O(nnz(row)), not O(columns), which is what makes refinement cheap. The composite's direction is the cluster centroid's direction, so cosine to the composite is cosine to the centroid.

docs.title: Criterion functions
docs.text: A criterion scores a whole partition from its composites. CLUTRO optimizes I2 = Σ_k ‖D_k‖, the sum of composite norms — the objective behind spherical k-means and CLUTO's default. Every criterion also prices a single-row move (Delta) so refinement can evaluate a candidate move in O(nnz(row)). The remaining CLUTO criteria (I1, E1, G1, G1′, H1, H2) are Phase 5 of the roadmap.

docs.title: Repeated bisection and the tree
docs.text: Rather than placing k centers at once, repeated bisection starts with one cluster and splits one cluster at a time: pick a cluster (the one whose split improves the criterion most, or the largest), run a 2-way spherical k-means from several seeded starts, keep the best split, repeat until k clusters exist. Each split is recorded in a tree, so the result is both a flat partition and a hierarchy you can re-cut (CutMaxSize, CutK) without re-clustering. Bisection is slower than direct k-means per cluster but far more robust on text, where direct k-means finds poor local optima.

docs.title: Refinement
docs.text: After bisection (or a direct k-way split), refinement visits rows in a seeded random order and moves each to the cluster that improves the criterion most, applying moves immediately, until a pass makes no move. This is CLUTO's rbr and the inner loop of direct.

docs.title: Result
docs.text: Fit returns a Result: labels, sizes, clusters, criterion value, the composites, the tree (for bisection), and — through the explain package — descriptions, discriminators, representatives and summaries that use the column labels you passed in.

docs.title: Evaluating Clusterings
docs.text: The evaluate package scores a clustering against known classes (external metrics) or from the data alone (internal metrics). Reference values are cross-checked against scikit-learn; see bench/reference/.

docs.title: External metrics — with ground truth
docs.text:
Function Range Meaning AdjustedRandIndex(x, y) ≈0 … 1 Agreement between two labelings corrected for chance; 1 = identical up to relabelling, ≈0 = independent. The standard way to compare two partitions. NormalizedMutualInformation(x, y) 0 … 1 I(x;y)/√(H(x)·H(y)) (scikit-learn's geometric average). Less sensitive than ARI to many small clusters. Purity(clusters, classes) 0 … 1 Fraction of rows whose cluster's majority class is their own class. Entropy(clusters, classes) 0 … 1 Size-weighted class entropy per cluster, normalized by log(#classes); 0 is pure. CLUTO reports purity and entropy.

Labels are []int32 of equal length; negative values are ordinary labels. cluto.ClassLabels turns an .rclass file's strings into ids.

docs.title: Internal metrics — without ground truth
docs.text:
All take the matrix, the labels and k, use Euclidean distance (on L2-normalized rows this ranks neighbours like cosine), and need 2 ≤ k < n.

Function Better Meaning Silhouette(m, labels, k, opts) higher, ≤ 1 Mean over rows of (b − a)/max(a, b): a = mean distance to own cluster, b = smallest mean distance to another. Singleton clusters score 0. Exact up to 10,000 rows, then a seeded sample (SampleAbove, Seed). DaviesBouldin(m, labels, k) lower, ≥ 0 Mean over clusters of the worst (s_i + s_j)/d(c_i, c_j); 0 is perfect; +Inf if two centroids coincide. CalinskiHarabasz(m, labels, k) higher Between-cluster over within-cluster dispersion, [B/(k−1)]/[W/(n−k)].

Internal metrics compare clusterings of the same data (different k, different algorithms). They are not comparable across datasets.

docs.title: Comparing with a reference clustering
docs.text:
rs, skips, err := golden.RunAll(ctx, corpora, golden.Options{Trials: 10, RowModel: matrix.RowL2})
golden.WriteTable(os.Stdout, rs)

The golden package re-clusters every <name> with a <name>.clustering.<k> file in a directory and reports ARI, NMI, and the I2 of both partitions — so you can tell "different but equally good" from "worse". clutro golden <dir> does the same from the command line. See Benchmarks and Validation for what it says about CLUTO.

docs.title: Explaining Clusters
docs.text: "Cluster 7 has 41 documents" is not an answer. The explain package — and the matching Result methods — say what a cluster is about, what sets it apart, which rows represent it, and how tight it is. Pass WithColumnLabels(vocab) to Fit and the features come back as words.

docs.title: Descriptive features
docs.text:
for _, f := range res.Describe(k, 5) {
    fmt.Printf("%s %.0f%%\n", f.Label, 100*f.Weight)
}

The columns that contribute most to the cluster's internal similarity: each column's share is D_k[j]² / ‖D_k‖², where D_k is the composite. Shares sum to 1 over all columns; Describe returns the top n. These are the features the cluster's rows have in common, including ones shared with every other cluster.

docs.title: Discriminating features
docs.text:
res.Discriminate(k, 5)

The columns that most separate the cluster from the rest of the rows: the contribution of each column to the gap between the cluster's internal similarity and its similarity to everything else, normalized to shares. Features that make the cluster more like the rest (such as a stopword present everywhere) are dropped, so the list says what is distinctive.

A cluster described by permiss access list token acl and discriminated by acl token permiss is about access control; a cluster described by the of and has not found anything, and its rows probably need better preprocessing (IDF weighting, stopword removal).

docs.title: Representatives
docs.text:
rows, sims := res.Representatives(k, 3)

The rows most similar to the cluster composite, best first — useful for labelling a cluster by its most central document.

docs.title: Summaries
docs.text:
for _, s := range res.Summaries() {
    fmt.Println(s.Cluster, s.Size, s.ISim, s.ISimDev, s.ESim, s.ESimDev)
}

For each cluster: size; ISim, the mean similarity of its rows to its own composite (tightness); ESim, the mean similarity of its rows to the composite of all other rows (separation); and their standard deviations. A good cluster has ISim well above ESim. These are CLUTO's -showsummaries figures.

docs.title: From the CLI
docs.text: clutro vcluster -showtree prints the bisection tree with each cluster's criterion contribution; per-cluster features from the CLI are planned alongside the describe command.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
The examples/ directory holds runnable programs that compile in CI: sparse (the README example, with explanations), dense (embeddings with spherical k-means and internal metrics), treecut (choosing k after the fit), cluto (migrating a CLUTO workflow), and hdbscan (a separate module feeding CLUTRO data to a density-based clusterer).

go run github.com/grokify/clutro/examples/sparse@latest

docs.title: The determinism contract
docs.text:
Same input, same options, same seed, same CLUTRO version ⇒ identical labels, independent of GOMAXPROCS or WithParallelism.

This is tested, not hoped for:

  • every random choice derives from the caller's seed through named sub-streams (rng.SubStream(seed, "kmeans", trial)), so trials, splits and refinement passes never share or race for random numbers;
  • parallel sweeps write to positions they own and partial sums are combined in worker-index order, never completion order;
  • ties break to the lowest cluster index with rows visited in index order;
  • a CI job runs the whole suite at GOMAXPROCS 1, 2 and 8, and tests compare labels across worker counts and against slow reference implementations (partition/reference) label for label.

Results may change between CLUTRO versions: an algorithmic improvement (such as greedy k-means++ seeding) changes which optimum a seed finds. The changelog records such changes.

docs.title: Float32 storage, float64 accumulation
docs.text:
Matrix values and row norms are float32; composites, dot products, criterion values and deltas are float64. Storage is half the size of float64 and cosine on L2-normalized rows is accurate to about 1e-7 relative, far below the differences that separate candidate assignments in practice.

Two consequences to know about:

  • a composite's norm is maintained incrementally from float32 row norms; Composite.Recompute resets accumulated rounding, and refinement calls it after every pass. A test bounds the drift after 20,000 adds and 10,000 removes at under 1e-6 relative;
  • feature shares from Describe sum to 1 within about 1e-7, and Discriminate drops shares below 1e-9 as rounding noise.

If you need float64 storage, implement matrix.Rows over your own data; the algorithms never assume CSR or Dense.

docs.title: Cancellation
docs.text: Every algorithm takes a context.Context and checks it once per outer iteration (k-means iteration, bisection step, refinement pass, harness corpus). Cancellation returns ctx.Err(); partial results are discarded.

docs.title: Non-finite input
docs.text: Constructors reject NaN and ±Inf values and out-of-range indices with matrix.ErrShape. Zero rows are allowed: they have similarity 0 to everything and stay wherever seeding put them.

docs.title: 1. Build a matrix
docs.text:
Rows are the things you want to cluster; columns are features. For text, rows are documents and columns are terms with TF-IDF weights; for embeddings, rows are vectors.

// Sparse, from (row, col, value) entries in any order.
m, err := matrix.NewCSRFromTriplets(nDocs, nTerms, triplets)
if err != nil {
    return err
}
// CLUTO-style preprocessing: IDF column weights, then unit-length rows.
if err := matrix.Preprocess(m, matrix.RowL2, matrix.ColIDF); err != nil {
    return err
}

// Dense, from row-major values.
d, err := matrix.NewDense(nRows, dims, values)
d.NormalizeRowsL2()

Both types implement matrix.Rows, which is all the algorithms need — so can your own store.

docs.title: 2. Fit
docs.text:
res, err := clutro.Fit(ctx, m,
    clutro.WithAlgorithm(clutro.RepeatedBisection), // the default
    clutro.WithClusters(20),
    clutro.WithRefinement(true),                    // rbr: refine after bisecting
    clutro.WithSeed(1),
    clutro.WithColumnLabels(vocab),                 // optional, for explanations
)

Defaults match CLUTO's: cosine similarity, the I2 criterion, 10 seeded trials per split, the best selection policy. res.Labels holds a cluster index per row; res.Clusters() the rows per cluster; res.Criterion the objective value.

docs.title: 3. Explain
docs.text:
for k := range res.K {
    fmt.Println(res.Sizes()[k], "rows")
    for _, f := range res.Describe(k, 5) {     // what the cluster is about
        fmt.Printf("  %s %.0f%%\n", f.Label, 100*f.Weight)
    }
    for _, f := range res.Discriminate(k, 3) { // what sets it apart
        fmt.Printf("  vs rest: %s\n", f.Label)
    }
    rows, sims := res.Representatives(k, 3)    // most central rows
    _ = rows; _ = sims
}
for _, s := range res.Summaries() {            // tightness and separation
    fmt.Println(s.Cluster, s.Size, s.ISim, s.ESim)
}

docs.title: 4. Choose k afterwards
docs.text:
Repeated bisection records every split, so you can re-cut without re-clustering:

tree := res.Tree()
byTwelve := tree.CutMaxSize(12) // clusters of about 12 rows or fewer
five := tree.CutK(5)

docs.title: 5. Evaluate
docs.text:
With ground truth:

ari, _ := evaluate.AdjustedRandIndex(res.Labels, truth)
nmi, _ := evaluate.NormalizedMutualInformation(res.Labels, truth)

Without:

sil, _ := evaluate.Silhouette(m, res.Labels, res.K, evaluate.SilhouetteOptions{})
db, _  := evaluate.DaviesBouldin(m, res.Labels, res.K)
ch, _  := evaluate.CalinskiHarabasz(m, res.Labels, res.K)

docs.title: 6. From the command line
docs.text:
clutro vcluster -clmethod=rbr -rowmodel=l2 -colmodel=idf docs.mat 20
clutro evaluate docs.mat.clustering.20 docs.rclass
clutro golden ./corpora     # compare against reference clusterings

The vcluster flags are CLUTO's; see CLUTO Compatibility.

docs.title: Release Notes v0.1.0
docs.text: Release Date: October 14, 2026

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
This is the initial release of CLUTRO, a pure-Go clustering toolkit for sparse and dense data built around the optimization-criterion approach of CLUTO: repeated bisection, spherical k-means, a pluggable criterion function, cluster explanation, and deterministic results — with no dependencies outside the Go standard library, for the library and the CLI alike.

The release covers Phases 1–4 of the roadmap. The remaining CLUTO criteria (I1, E1, G1, G1′, H1, H2), per-level refinement and agglomerative clustering follow in v0.2.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
go get github.com/grokify/clutro@v0.1.0
go install github.com/grokify/clutro/cmd/clutro@v0.1.0

docs.title: Matrices and similarity
docs.text: matrix.CSR (sparse, float32 values, uint32 columns) and matrix.Dense behind one Rows interface; L2 row normalization and IDF column weighting (matrix.Preprocess, CLUTO's -rowmodel/-colmodel); merge-join dot products; cluster composite vectors with O(nnz) incremental add/remove. metric.Cosine and metric.Euclidean.

docs.title: Criterion-driven clustering
docs.text: clutro.Fit with RepeatedBisection (CLUTO rb; rbr with WithRefinement), Direct and KMeans (spherical under cosine), all optimizing the I2 criterion with greedy k-means++ seeding and multiple seeded trials. Repeated bisection returns its tree, so CutMaxSize and CutK re-partition without re-clustering. Defaults match CLUTO's.

docs.title: Explanation
docs.text: Describe (descriptive features), Discriminate (what sets a cluster apart), Representatives (most central rows) and Summaries (size, ISim, ESim) — CLUTO's -showfeatures and -showsummaries as library calls, in words when column labels are given.

docs.title: Evaluation
docs.text: External: adjusted Rand index, NMI, purity, entropy. Internal: silhouette (sampled above 10,000 rows), Davies–Bouldin, Calinski–Harabasz. Reference values cross-checked against scikit-learn.

docs.title: Determinism
docs.text: Same input, options, seed and version give identical labels regardless of GOMAXPROCS. Random choices come from named seeded sub-streams, parallel reductions are order-independent, and the optimized paths are tested against slow reference implementations; a CI job runs the suite under several GOMAXPROCS values.

docs.title: CLUTO compatibility
docs.text: Readers and writers for CLUTO's matrix, label and clustering files; the clutro vcluster command with CLUTO's flag names and defaults; and a golden harness that re-clusters CLUTO corpora and compares. On 103 real text corpora, CLUTRO's partitions score 1.0007× (rb) to 1.033× (rbr) of CLUTO's on the criterion CLUTO optimized; eight numeric-only corpora are published as fixtures with an asserted agreement band.

docs.title: Interoperability
docs.text: examples/hdbscan (a separate module) feeds CLUTRO matrices to github.com/kinn-gg/hdbscan for density-based clustering, which CLUTRO deliberately does not reimplement.

docs.title: Known Limitations
docs.text:
• Only the I2 criterion is implemented; -crfun accepts nothing else yet.
  • rbr refines the final partition, not after every bisection as CLUTO does (a v0.2 option).
  • No agglomerative clustering, graph (scluster) input or feature-subspace cluster selection.
  • Per-cluster features are a library call, not yet a CLI command.
  • Row and column labels in .rlabel/.clabel files are read but the CLI does not yet print features by name.

docs.title: CLUTRO — Implementation Plan (PLAN)
docs.text:
Status: Draft Date: 2026-10-14 Repo: github.com/grokify/clutro

This plan sequences the work defined in the PRD and TRD. Roadmap items and phase membership are tracked in ROADMAP.md; this document explains ordering, dependencies, and verification per phase.

docs.title: Guiding constraints
docs.text:
• Correct before fast, fast before broad. Phase 1 proves the sparse primitives and determinism machinery with benchmarks; algorithms are added only on top of measured primitives; new algorithm families wait for v0.2+.
  • Every phase leaves main building with CGO_ENABLED=0, tested with -race, lint-clean, and with the README example compiling.
  • Library packages stay dependency-free. A go.mod diff that adds a library dependency is a design review, not a routine change.
  • Determinism is enforced from Phase 1, so later algorithms inherit it instead of retrofitting it.
  • Public from the first commit: generic technical commit messages, synthetic fixtures only, no private data or paths.
  • Verify dependency versions (cobra) at adoption time.

docs.title: Phase 1 — Matrix, metric, RNG foundation
docs.text:
Goal: matrix.CSR / matrix.Dense behind Rows, cosine and Euclidean similarity, composite vectors with incremental update, deterministic RNG sub-streams and a bounded pool with ordered reduction — all benchmarked.

Order of work:

  1. Module scaffold: go.mod, LICENSE (Apache-2.0), README, CI workflows (test with -race, lint, CGO_ENABLED=0 cross-build matrix, determinism job stub), CHANGELOG.json.
  2. matrix/: SparseVec, Rows, CSR (from triplets, from row slices), Dense, NormalizeRowsL2, cached norms, sparse·sparse and sparse·dense dot products (merge-join), Composite with Add/Remove and norm maintenance. Benchmarks for dot products at 100/1k/10k nnz.
  3. metric/: Similarity interface; Cosine (dot on normalized rows, with a slow path for unnormalized), Euclidean as distance and as similarity.
  4. internal/rng/: PCG64 sub-streams SubStream(seed, name, idx), seeded shuffle; internal/par/: bounded pool, positional writes, worker-order reduction.
  5. testdata/gen: planted-structure generator (sparse and dense) used by every later phase.

Verify: benchmarks recorded in bench/README.md; float32-storage/float64-accumulation decision confirmed by a precision test on 1M-nnz composites (PRD §9.2); go test -race clean.

docs.title: Phase 2 — Criterion I2, k-means family, repeated bisection
docs.text:
Goal: clutro.Fit with KMeans, SphericalKMeans, RepeatedBisection (+WithRefinement), Direct, optimizing I2, returning a Result with a Tree.

Order of work:

  1. criterion/: interface, I2 with Value and Delta (TRD §5.4), numeric tests against hand-computed fixtures.
  2. partition/kmeans.go: k-means++ init with trials, Lloyd, spherical variant; parallel assignment via internal/par.
  3. partition/bisect.go: 2-way bisection with trials; selection policies best and largest; Tree construction; CutMaxSize, CutK.
  4. partition/refine.go: incremental refinement using Criterion.Delta; Direct = k-way init + refine.
  5. clutro.go, options.go, result.go, errors.go: facade, validation, option defaults mirroring CLUTO (rb, i2, cos, best, 10 trials, 20 iterations).
  6. Density interop example (examples/hdbscan): adapt matrix.Dense to kinn-gg/hdbscan's Dense64, and build a kNN cosine similarity graph from CSR rows and convert it to its SparsePrecomputed distance graph. Lives under examples/ with its own go.mod so the library keeps zero dependencies.

Depends on: Phase 1. Verify: planted-structure ARI ≥ 0.95 for all algorithms; determinism job passes (GOMAXPROCS 1 vs 8, sequential vs parallel trials); TRD §10 10k-row target met; README example compiles from examples/sparse.

docs.title: Phase 3 — CLUTO formats, CLI, golden-set validation
docs.text:
Goal: clutro vcluster is a drop-in for CLUTO's vcluster on the supported flags, and agreement with CLUTO's own results is measured.

Order of work:

  1. cluto/: readers/writers for sparse/dense matrices (1-based columns), .clabel, .rlabel, .rclass, .clustering.<k>; round-trip tests; malformed-input tests.
  2. evaluate/ external metrics: ARI, NMI, purity, entropy.
  3. cmd/clutro: vcluster with the TRD §7 flags, -json; evaluate; exit codes and stderr progress.
  4. Golden-set harness (bench/golden): run every CLUTO corpus in a directory (the public testdata/cluto/ subset in CI; the owner's full set privately), compute ARI and matched label agreement vs CLUTO's .clustering.<k> under -colmodel none and idf, print a table; inspect the worst corpora by hand; set and assert the lower band. The published subset is numeric-only and renamed (TRD §9.3).
  5. Row/column preprocessing flags (-rowmodel l2, -colmodel idf) so raw count matrices can be clustered like CLUTO does.

Depends on: Phase 2. Verify: a CLUTO script with the binary name swapped produces a .clustering.<k> file with ARI in the accepted band; clutro evaluate matches scikit-learn's ARI/NMI on fixtures to 1e-9.

docs.title: Phase 4 — Explanation, internal metrics, v0.1 release
docs.text:
Goal: Every cluster can be explained and every run can be scored without truth labels; v0.1.0 tagged.

Order of work:

  1. explain/: descriptive and discriminating features with cumulative share, representatives, summaries (ISim/ESim); column labels via option; -showfeatures, -showsummaries, describe command.
  2. evaluate/ internal metrics: silhouette (seeded sampling above 10k rows), Davies–Bouldin, Calinski–Harabasz; scikit-learn cross-check script in bench/reference/.
  3. examples/: sparse text with explanation, dense embeddings, tree cut, CLUTO migration — all compiled in CI.
  4. Documentation: algorithm reference with citations and the "differences from CLUTO" page; benchmarks page from bench/ runs on the 10k/100k workloads.
  5. Release: CHANGELOG, coverage badge, v0.1.0 after CI passes; the first consumer switches from a local replace to the tagged version.

Depends on: Phases 2–3. Verify: PRD §8 v0.1 rows; a cluster of a real text corpus reads sensibly from its top-5 descriptive features in manual review.

docs.title: Phase 5 — v0.2: full criterion family and refinement fidelity
docs.text:
Goal: CLUTO's optimization vocabulary is complete: I1, E1, G1, G1′, H1, H2 with incremental deltas; per-level refinement in rbr; agglomerative clustering driven by the same criteria.

Order of work:

  1. criterion/: I1, E1, G1, G1′ with Delta; H1, H2 as ratios with delta via numerator/denominator tracking; numeric tests per criterion; -crfun wired.
  2. rbr per-level refinement option (refine after every bisection, as CLUTO does); comparison against end-only refinement on the golden set.
  3. hierarchical/: agglomerative merging that maximizes the chosen criterion (CLUTO agglo), dendrogram output, CutK; -fulltree building the hierarchy on top of rb leaves.
  4. Jaccard and Pearson similarities; -sim extended.
  5. Benchmarks and golden-set re-run per criterion; v0.2.0.

Depends on: Phase 4. Decision point: whether graph-input clustering (scluster) is next (v0.3) depends on demand from consumers; density methods are only scheduled if a concrete user needs them.

docs.title: CLUTRO — Product Requirements Document (PRD)
docs.text: Status: Draft Date: 2026-10-14 Repo: github.com/grokify/clutro

docs.title: 1. Summary
docs.text:
CLUTRO is a pure-Go clustering toolkit for sparse, dense, and (later) graph-structured data. It brings the ideas that made CLUTO (Karypis, 2002) the standard tool for document clustering — criterion-driven partitional clustering, repeated bisection, spherical k-means, and cluster interpretation — to a modern Go API with deterministic results, context.Context cancellation, and no cgo.

CLUTRO is a clustering engine, not an ML framework. It takes a matrix and returns an assignment plus an explanation. Embedding generation, vector databases, LLM calls, and visualization are the caller's responsibility.

Naming: the project is CLUTRO (all caps, like CLUTO, LLVM); the Go module, package, and executable are clutro. No acronym expansion. CLUTRO is an independent clean-room implementation of published algorithms and is not affiliated with, derived from, or endorsed by the Karypis lab or the University of Minnesota; the README and every release note say so.

docs.title: 2. Problem
docs.text:
• Go has no sparse-aware clustering engine. Existing packages (mpraski/clusters, muesli/kmeans, pa-m/sklearn) take dense [][]float64, are unmaintained, and cannot hold a 100k × 500k TF-IDF matrix. james-bowman/nlp has sparse TF-IDF/LSA but no clustering and has been dormant since 2021. go-nlp/dmmclust is a short-text topic model, not a general clusterer.
  • CLUTO is unavailable. It was distributed as research-use binaries for 2000s platforms, is copyrighted and not open-source, and its clustering behaviour (repeated bisection optimizing I2 over cosine similarity) has no faithful reimplementation in any language that a Go program can call without cgo or a subprocess.
  • Modern clustering libraries optimize the wrong thing for text. Lloyd's k-means minimizes Euclidean SSE; for L2-normalized sparse vectors the right objective is a similarity-based criterion (I2, H2, …), and the right algorithm is bisection with refinement. Few libraries expose criterion choice at all.
  • Nobody explains clusters. "Cluster 7 has 41 documents" is not an answer; "cluster 7 is about ldap, directory, authentication" is. CLUTO's descriptive/discriminating features have no mainstream equivalent.

docs.title: 3. Target users
docs.text:
User Need Go developers clustering text (TF-IDF, BM25 vectors) Sparse input, cosine, sensible defaults, deterministic output, an explanation per cluster Developers clustering embeddings (OpenAI, local models) Dense input, spherical k-means / bisection, quality metrics, no cgo Former CLUTO users The same algorithms and vocabulary (rb, rbr, i2, cos, .mat/.clabel), a drop-in CLI, documented differences Library authors A small dependency-free core they can embed (search engines, dedup, log grouping, glossary/related-items features) Researchers Correct criterion functions with citations, reproducibility, benchmarks against reference implementations

The first consumer is a private text application that groups related items across ~100 topic corpora of up to ~8k sparse documents each; it previously used CLUTO and supplies the golden corpus described in §9.1.

docs.title: 4. Goals (V1 = v0.1 → v0.2)
docs.text:
• G1 — Sparse-first. CSR matrices are the primary input; dense is supported through the same interface. A 100k-row, 10M-nnz corpus clusters in memory on a laptop.
  • G2 — Criterion-driven partitional clustering. Repeated bisection (rb), repeated bisection with refinement (rbr), direct k-way (direct), and k-means/spherical k-means, optimizing a selectable criterion. v0.1 ships I2; v0.2 adds I1, E1, G1, G1′, H1, H2 with incremental delta updates for refinement.
  • G3 — Interpretation. Descriptive and discriminating features per cluster (CLUTO -showfeatures), representative rows (closest to centroid), per-cluster internal/external similarity statistics (-showsummaries-style).
  • G4 — Determinism contract. Same input, same options, same seed, same CLUTRO version ⇒ identical labels, independent of GOMAXPROCS. Tested in CI.
  • G5 — CLUTO file compatibility. Read/write CLUTO sparse and dense matrix files, .clabel/.rlabel, and .clustering.<k>; the clutro vcluster CLI uses CLUTO's flag vocabulary so existing scripts port by changing the binary name.
  • G6 — Evaluation. External metrics (adjusted Rand index, NMI, purity, entropy) and internal metrics (silhouette, Davies–Bouldin, Calinski–Harabasz) so users can compare runs and so CI can compare CLUTRO with reference implementations.
  • G7 — Engine, not framework. Zero third-party dependencies in the library packages (standard library only; cobra in cmd/ only). No cgo. context.Context on every long operation.
  • G8 — Twenty-line example. A working sparse-clustering example with explanation fits in 20 lines of Go.

docs.title: 5. Non-goals
docs.text:
• Not in V1: graph clustering (scluster equivalent, multilevel partitioning), agglomerative/divisive hierarchical with arbitrary linkage, streaming/incremental clustering. These are roadmap candidates for v0.3+, each judged on its own merits.
  • Density methods (DBSCAN/HDBSCAN/OPTICS) are not planned at all. A dependency-free, deterministic Go HDBSCAN already exists (github.com/kinn-gg/hdbscan, a port of scikit-learn-contrib's hdbscan with parity fixtures). CLUTRO documents how to hand it a dense matrix or a CLUTRO-built similarity graph rather than reimplementing it.
  • Never: embedding generation, tokenization/TF-IDF (the caller or a sibling text package produces the matrix), vector-database integration, LLM-generated cluster descriptions, GUI/visualization. CLUTRO may document how to combine with such tools; it does not depend on them.
  • No binary or API compatibility with CLUTO. Algorithmic fidelity (same objective, same algorithm, comparable results) is the goal, not reproducing a C interface or matching CLUTO's random number stream.

docs.title: 6. Core concepts
docs.text:
• Matrix — rows are objects, columns are features. matrix.CSR (sparse) and matrix.Dense implement one read interface used by every algorithm. Rows are typically L2-normalized so cosine similarity is a dot product.
  • Similarity vs distance — algorithms are written against a metric.Similarity; distances are wrapped. Cosine and Euclidean in V1.
  • Criterion function — a global objective over a partition, e.g. I2 = Σ_k ‖D_k‖ (sum of composite-vector norms, maximize). The algorithm's job is to find a partition that optimizes it; criterion.Delta gives the change from moving one row, which is what refinement needs.
  • Repeated bisection — start with one cluster; k−1 times, choose a cluster (largest, or the one whose split improves the criterion most), split it 2-way with several seeded trials, keep the best. Produces a binary tree as a by-product.
  • Refinement — after bisection or direct clustering, iteratively move rows between clusters while the criterion improves (CLUTO rbr, and the inner loop of direct).
  • Explanation — for each cluster, the features that contribute most to within-cluster similarity (descriptive) and most to separation from other clusters (discriminating); plus rows nearest the centroid.
  • Result — labels, sizes, criterion value, per-cluster statistics, the bisection tree when applicable, and accessors for explanation.

docs.title: 7. Key user flows
docs.text:
// Sparse text clustering, explained
m := matrix.NewCSRFromTriplets(nRows, nCols, triplets)
m.NormalizeRowsL2()
res, err := clutro.Fit(ctx, m, clutro.WithAlgorithm(clutro.RepeatedBisection),
    clutro.WithClusters(50), clutro.WithRefinement(true), clutro.WithSeed(1))
for k := range res.K() {
    fmt.Println(res.Size(k), res.Describe(k, 5), res.Representatives(k, 3))
}

// Dense embeddings
d := matrix.NewDense(nRows, 1536, values)
res, err := clutro.Fit(ctx, d, clutro.WithAlgorithm(clutro.SphericalKMeans), clutro.WithClusters(20))

// Pick k after the fact from the bisection tree
tree := res.Tree()            // nil unless rb/rbr
labels := tree.CutMaxSize(12) // ≈12 rows per leaf

# CLUTO migration
clutro vcluster -clmethod=rbr -crfun=i2 -sim=cos -showfeatures docs.mat 50
# → docs.mat.clustering.50, features on stdout
clutro evaluate --truth labels.txt docs.mat.clustering.50   # ARI, NMI, purity, entropy

docs.title: 8. Success metrics
docs.text: Dimension Target Correctness I2 and refinement validated against (a) hand-computable fixtures, (b) a 103-corpus CLUTO golden set (ARI reported per corpus; band set in Phase 3), (c) scikit-learn for k-means/spherical k-means on dense data Reproducibility CI job runs the suite at GOMAXPROCS=1 and =8 and diffs labels: must be identical Performance 100k × 10M-nnz CSR, rb, k=100: < 60 s on a laptop in v0.1; benchmark numbers published per release, never claimed in advance Scale Benchmarks at 10k, 100k, 1M rows; memory ≤ 3× the CSR size Usability README example ≤ 20 lines and compiles in CI (examples/) Portability CGO_ENABLED=0 builds on linux/darwin/windows, amd64/arm64 Adoption The first consumer in production on CLUTRO; at least one external Go project importing it within a year of v1.0

docs.title: 9. Open questions
docs.text:
1. ~~Golden corpus publication~~ — decided: a numeric-only subset is published under testdata/cluto/ under the repository license (see TRD §9.3): CLUTO sparse matrices and .clustering.<k> files with row and column labels stripped and corpora renamed corpus-NN. No vocabulary, no text, no identifiers; the full set stays with its owner and runs there.
  2. Float width. float32 storage with float64 accumulation is the proposal (halves memory, adequate for cosine on normalized rows). Confirm after the Phase 1 benchmark.
  3. Generics. A Number type parameter would let callers choose width but complicates every signature. Proposal: no generics in v0.1; revisit if a user needs float64 storage.
  4. License. Apache-2.0 as proposed; confirm before the first public push (MIT is the alternative).

docs.title: CLUTRO — Technical Requirements Document (TRD)
docs.text: Status: Draft Date: 2026-10-14 Repo: github.com/grokify/clutro

docs.title: 1. Architecture overview
docs.text:
A small, layered, dependency-free library. Every algorithm is written against two interfaces — a row-readable matrix and a criterion — so adding a criterion, a metric, or a matrix type never touches the algorithms.

                 clutro (facade: Fit, Options, Result)
                               │
   ┌───────────┬───────────────┼────────────────┬──────────────┐
   │ partition │  hierarchical │   explain      │   evaluate   │
   │ kmeans    │  (v0.2)       │ describe/      │ ARI NMI      │
   │ skmeans   │  agglo        │ discriminate/  │ purity       │
   │ bisect    │               │ representatives│ silhouette … │
   │ direct    │               │                │              │
   └─────┬─────┴───────┬───────┴───────┬────────┴──────┬───────┘
         │             │               │               │
   ┌─────▼─────────────▼───────────────▼───────────────▼───────┐
   │ criterion   I2 (v0.1) · I1 E1 G1 G1′ H1 H2 (v0.2)          │
   │ metric      Cosine · Euclidean · (Jaccard, Pearson later)  │
   │ matrix      CSR · Dense · Rows interface · composite vecs  │
   │ internal/rng  PCG, per-trial streams, deterministic reduce │
   └────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
         ▲                                   ▲
   cluto/ (file formats: .mat .clabel .rlabel .clustering)
   cmd/clutro (CLI: vcluster, evaluate, describe)   examples/   bench/

Design rules:

  • Library packages import only the standard library. cobra is permitted in cmd/clutro only. No cgo anywhere.
  • Algorithms never allocate per row in the inner loop. Work buffers are sized once per call; sparse dot products are merge-joins over sorted column indices.
  • Determinism is a tested contract, not an accident: every random choice derives from the caller's seed through named sub-streams, and every parallel reduction is order-independent or re-sorted before use.
  • context.Context on every exported operation that iterates; cancellation is checked once per outer iteration and returns ctx.Err() wrapped with progress information.
  • Errors are returned, never logged. Invariant violations (NaN in a normalized row, k > rows) are returned as typed errors from validation before any work starts; internal impossibilities panic.

docs.title: 2. Module and dependencies
docs.text:
• Module: github.com/grokify/clutro, Go 1.26+
  • Library dependencies: none
  • CLI: github.com/spf13/cobra
  • Dev/CI: golangci-lint, gocoverbadge; Python + scikit-learn only inside bench/reference/ for cross-validation scripts, never imported by Go code
  • Verify versions at adoption time (go list -m -versions); do not assume versions in this document are current.

docs.title: 4. Core types
docs.text:
// matrix
type Rows interface {
    NumRows() int
    NumCols() int
    Row(i int) SparseVec          // for Dense: a view with Idx = 0..n-1 (no allocation beyond the view)
    RowNorm(i int) float32        // cached L2 norm
}
type SparseVec struct { Idx []uint32; Val []float32 }   // Idx sorted ascending
type CSR struct { rowPtr []uint32; idx []uint32; val []float32; norms []float32; nCols int }
type Dense struct { data []float32; nCols int; norms []float32 }

// composite vector of a cluster: D_k = Σ rows ∈ S_k, kept dense (len = NumCols) for speed; sparse fallback when NumCols is huge
type Composite struct { Sum []float64; N int; Norm float64 }

// metric
type Similarity interface {
    Sim(a, b SparseVec, normA, normB float32) float64
    RowToComposite(r SparseVec, normR float32, c *Composite) float64
    Name() string
}

// criterion
type Criterion interface {
    Name() string
    Value(comps []Composite) float64                 // global objective
    Maximize() bool
    Delta(from, to *Composite, r SparseVec, normR float32) float64 // change if r moves from→to; must be O(nnz(r))
}

// partition
type Assignment struct { Labels []int32; K int }
type Tree struct { Root *Node } ; type Node struct { Rows []int32; Left, Right *Node; Criterion float64 }

// facade
type Result struct { /* Assignment, Composites, Tree (optional), Options, stats */ }
func Fit(ctx context.Context, m matrix.Rows, opts ...Option) (*Result, error)

The Rows interface is deliberately narrow so a caller with a custom store (e.g. memory-mapped vectors) can implement it.

docs.title: 5.1 k-means and spherical k-means
docs.text:
• Init: k-means++ with trials candidate sets; each trial has its own RNG sub-stream rng.SubStream(seed, "kmeans++", trial).
  • Lloyd iterations until no label changes or maxIter (default 20, matching CLUTO's -niter). Spherical variant normalizes centroids and uses cosine.
  • Tie-breaking: lowest cluster index wins; rows are visited in index order; parallel assignment writes to a per-row slot so order never affects results.

docs.title: 5.2 Repeated bisection (rb)
docs.text:
CLUTO's default and the method of record for text:

  1. Start with all rows in one cluster.
  2. Repeat k−1 times: choose the cluster to split by selection policy — largest (most rows) or best (the split that most improves the criterion; computed lazily and cached per cluster, invalidated on split). Default best, as CLUTO.
  3. Bisect it with 2-way spherical k-means from trials seeded starts (default 10, CLUTO -ntrials), each run to convergence; keep the bisection with the best criterion value. Clusters with < 2 rows are not split.
  4. Record both children in the Tree.

The result is both a flat k-way assignment and a binary tree whose leaves are the k clusters; Tree.CutMaxSize(n) and Tree.CutK(k') re-partition without re-clustering.

docs.title: 5.3 Refinement (rbr, and direct)
docs.text: Given an assignment, repeat until no improvement or maxIter: visit rows in a seeded random order; for each row compute criterion.Delta to every other cluster (O(k · nnz(r)) with composite vectors kept dense); move if the best delta > 0 and apply the move immediately (incremental composite update). rbr = rb then refine the final k-way partition (CLUTO also refines at each bisection level when -rbr; v0.1 refines at the end, the per-level variant is an option). direct = k-means++ initial k-way split then refine.

docs.title: 5.4 Criterion I2
docs.text:
For cosine on L2-normalized rows, cluster k's composite D_k = Σ_{i∈S_k} d_i, and

  • I2 = Σ_k ‖D_k‖ (maximize).
  • Delta(from, to, r) = (‖D_to + r‖ − ‖D_to‖) + (‖D_from − r‖ − ‖D_from‖), computed from the stored norms and two sparse dot products: ‖D ± r‖² = ‖D‖² ± 2 D·r + ‖r‖².

v0.2 criteria (same interface, same delta discipline; definitions per Zhao & Karypis, Machine Learning 55, 2004):

Criterion Objective Sense I1 Σ_k (1/n_k) ‖D_k‖² max I2 Σ_k ‖D_k‖ max E1 Σ_k n_k · (D_kᵀD)/‖D_k‖ min G1 Σ_k (D_kᵀ D)/‖D_k‖² (cut / internal) min G1′ Σ_k n_k² · (D_kᵀ D)/‖D_k‖² min H1 I1 / E1 max H2 I2 / E1 max

where D is the composite of all rows.

docs.title: 5.5 Parallelism and determinism
docs.text:
• The distance/similarity sweep of each iteration is split across a bounded pool (WithParallelism(n), default runtime.NumCPU()); each worker writes results for its row range into pre-allocated slices, so the merge is positional and order-free.
  • Any reduction that sums floats across workers sums per-worker partials in worker-index order (fixed), never in completion order.
  • Trials run sequentially by default (their RNG streams are independent, so running them in parallel is a pure optimization and must produce the same winner; a test asserts this).
  • RNG: PCG64 (math/rand/v2 PCG), sub-streams derived by hashing (seed, name, index).

docs.title: 5.6 Explanation (explain/)
docs.text:
• Descriptive features of cluster k: columns j ranked by their contribution to the within-cluster similarity, D_k[j]² / ‖D_k‖²; report the top-n and the cumulative share (CLUTO prints enough features to reach a percentage).
  • Discriminating features: columns ranked by D_k[j]·(D[j] − D_k[j]) contribution to the between-cluster similarity, i.e. what most separates k from the rest.
  • Representatives: rows with highest RowToComposite similarity to their cluster's composite.
  • Summaries: per cluster, size, mean internal similarity (ISim), mean external similarity (ESim), and their standard deviations.

Feature names come from an optional []string column-label slice (CLUTO .clabel) supplied via WithColumnLabels; otherwise indices are reported.

docs.title: 6. CLUTO file formats (cluto/)
docs.text:
• Sparse matrix: header nrows ncols nnz, then one row per line of col val pairs with 1-based columns. Dense: nrows ncols then values.
  • Labels: .clabel (one column name per line), .rlabel (row names), .rclass (true class per row, for evaluation).
  • Clustering: <matrix>.clustering.<k>, one 0-based cluster id per row, -1 for unassigned.
  • Readers are streaming and validate shape; writers are deterministic.

docs.title: 7. CLI (cmd/clutro)
docs.text:
clutro vcluster [flags] <matrix> <k>
  -clmethod rb|rbr|direct|kmeans|skmeans   (default rb)
  -crfun    i2|i1|e1|g1|g1p|h1|h2         (default i2; non-i2 from v0.2)
  -sim      cos|euclid                     (default cos)
  -cstype   best|largest                   (default best)
  -ntrials N  -niter N  -seed N  -parallel N
  -rowmodel none|l2      -colmodel none|idf  (preprocessing, CLUTO vocabulary)
  -showfeatures [-nfeatures N]  -showsummaries  -showtree
  -clustfile PATH  -fulltree PATH  -json
clutro evaluate [-truth FILE | -rclass] <matrix> <clustering>
clutro describe [-nfeatures N] <matrix> <clustering>

Flag names deliberately mirror CLUTO's so that scripts port by substitution; -json emits the full Result for programmatic use.

docs.title: 8. Evaluation (evaluate/)
docs.text: External (need truth labels): adjusted Rand index, normalized mutual information, purity, entropy (CLUTO's two). Internal: silhouette (sampled above 10k rows, sample seeded), Davies–Bouldin, Calinski–Harabasz. All pure functions over []int32 labels and Rows.

docs.title: 9. Validation strategy
docs.text:
1. Reference oracle in-tree. partition/reference holds slow, obviously-correct implementations of k-means, bisection, and refinement (no parallelism, no incremental deltas, dense composites). The optimized paths must reproduce the reference's labels exactly on every fixture; tie-breaking rules are defined by the reference and documented. (Pattern borrowed from kinn-gg/hdbscan's Reference vs Exact split.)
  2. Hand-computable fixtures (≤ 12 rows): I2 values, deltas, and the exact bisection result are asserted numerically.
  3. Planted-structure corpora (testdata/gen): synthetic sparse matrices with known clusters; ARI ≥ 0.95 asserted for rb/rbr/direct.
  4. CLUTO golden set: CLUTO's own inputs and outputs for real corpora — the sparse matrix vcluster read and the .clustering.<k> it wrote. The published subset in testdata/cluto/ is numeric only: no .clabel/.rlabel, corpora renamed corpus-NN, chosen to span sizes (three of ~100–300 rows, three of ~500–1,500, two of ~3,000–6,500 rows with up to ~100k nonzeros) with their original k, under 2 MB total, listed in SHA256SUMS.json. Because CLUTO's RNG stream cannot be reproduced, agreement is measured with ARI (and per-row label agreement after Hungarian matching), reported per corpus as a table in CI; an accepted lower band is set in Phase 3 after inspection and then asserted. The harness also runs with -colmodel none and idf and reports both, since CLUTO's effective default on these files is established empirically rather than assumed. The full ~100-corpus set stays with its owner, who runs the same harness privately.
  5. scikit-learn cross-check as pinned parity fixtures: bench/reference/ scripts generate testdata/parity/*.json (named per case: kmeans_fixed_init, skmeans_duplicates_ties, silhouette_sampled, …) from a pinned scikit-learn version recorded in NOTICE, with a SHA256SUMS.json; Go tests consume the JSON and never call Python. k-means and spherical k-means with identical init centers must converge to identical labels; silhouette/DB/CH/ARI/NMI values must match to 1e-6.
  6. Determinism job: the whole suite at GOMAXPROCS=1 and GOMAXPROCS=8, labels diffed.

docs.title: 10. Performance targets and benchmarks
docs.text:
Workload Target (v0.1, laptop, 8 cores) 10k rows × 1M nnz, rb k=50 < 2 s 100k rows × 10M nnz, rb k=100 < 60 s 100k rows × 10M nnz, rbr k=100 < 120 s 1M rows × 100M nnz, rb k=500 completes in < 30 min; memory ≤ 3× CSR size Dense 100k × 1536, skmeans k=100 < 60 s

Published numbers come from bench/ runs recorded in release notes; the table above is the target, not a claim.

docs.title: 11. Testing and quality gates
docs.text:
• go test ./... with race detector; coverage badge; golangci-lint clean; CGO_ENABLED=0 cross-build matrix in CI.
  • examples/ compile and run in CI; the README example is examples/sparse/main.go verbatim.
  • API stability: pre-v1 may break between minors with a CHANGELOG entry; v1.0 freezes clutro, matrix, metric, criterion, evaluate, cluto public APIs.

docs.title: 12. Publication hygiene
docs.text: The repo is public from its first push. Commit messages, fixtures, and docs contain no private project data, credentials, or internal paths. The CLUTO golden corpus is referenced by name only until the owner publishes a subset; CI fetches nothing private.
